narrative.overview:
Everything for the trip in your pocket, calm and always to hand. Unterwegs is opened on a platform, at a hotel desk or in a temple without signal, by people who know their phone but not this app. So the design is calm, native and quietly warm: the platform's own controls (SwiftUI on iOS, Material 3 on Android) do most of the work, and personality comes from one warm accent and the trip's own photos. It is flat and layered, not decorative, and nothing competes with the information you need right now.

Density is that of a system settings screen: grouped lists of rows, each row one fact with a tinted icon, a value and a secondary line. The one exception is the collection hero (`CollectionHero`) on the home screen, a full-bleed photo card that is the app's only "loud" moment.

Direction, not yet decided: the current look is deliberately plain, and the owner finds it a bit too boring. Future work may make it more playful. That should come from the trip itself (photos, locations, moments like "Heute" and the countdown) and stay within the accessibility rules below, rather than from decoration added on top of the native controls.
keyCharacteristics: Native grouped lists on a grey background; white (or near-black) rows.
One accent, Terracotta, for icons, the selected state and calls to action.
The trip's photos carry the colour; the chrome stays neutral.
Every text size follows the system and the app's own text-size setting.
Light, dark and a "Mehr Kontrast" palette for each.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Terracotta is the only UI accent. Blue and green exist only to tell map points apart; they never appear on buttons, icons or text.

rules.name: The Contrast Twin Rule
rules.body: Every colour the UI uses has a "Mehr Kontrast" twin in `useColors()` (darker in light mode, lighter in dark mode). A new colour is not done until its twin exists.

rules.name: The Dynamic Type Rule
rules.body: Sizes are written as plain numbers, but on iOS `src/ui/Text` maps each to the nearest Dynamic Type style (17 → body, 15 → subheadline, 13 → footnote …), and on Android text follows the font scale. Never set a size that ignores the user's text size; React Native text outside native rows uses `rnTextScale` (see the hero's `Label`).

rules.name: The Fixed-Box Cap Rule
rules.body: Text inside a fixed-height box (the hero card) may scale at most 1.4×; everywhere else text grows without a cap and the layout grows with it.

rules.name: The Flat List Rule
rules.body: Lists and sheets never get shadows; only something floating over a map or photo may.

dos: Do use the platform's own controls (`@expo/ui`) first; React Native views only where no native one exists (hero, map, gallery, day strip, thumbnails).
Do take colours from `useColors()` so light, dark and "Mehr Kontrast" all work; add the contrast twin with any new colour.
Do give every row a leading icon in Terracotta and a plain-language secondary line.
Do let text grow: check new screens at "Riesig" and with bold text on both platforms.
Do honour reduced motion: no stack animation, no image fades.
donts: Don't use blue or green outside the map.
Don't add shadows to list content or cards in a list.
Don't set fixed font sizes that bypass Dynamic Type or the app's text-size setting.
Don't rely on icons alone: every action has a text label (Android toolbar icons excepted, with an accessibility label).
Don't show the Japan trip's real data in published screenshots or marketing.
